target.title: fix(macos): host the dashboard sidebar toggle beside back/forward in the titlebar
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the Mac app's dashboard window shows the Control UI's floating sidebar-expand button as a bordered box floating directly under the traffic-light window controls whenever the navigation sidebar is collapsed. It crowds the window controls, uses web-style chrome (border, panel background) that clashes with the native titlebar, and sits in a different row than the native back/forward buttons introduced in #104328.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dashboard window already hosts native back/forward controls in a leading titlebar accessory; the natural macOS home for a sidebar toggle is that same row (Safari ordering: sidebar toggle, then history controls). A web-rendered control cannot live in that row because the AppKit drag regions over the titlebar strip swallow its clicks, so the toggle becomes a native `NSButton` that bridges into the Control UI:

- `DashboardWindowController` adds a borderless `sidebar.leading` button ahead of back/forward, gives the whole accessory group slightly wider insets/spacing, and dispatches `openclaw:native-toggle-sidebar` into the page.
- The Control UI (`app-host.ts`) listens for that event and runs the existing `toggleNavigationSurface()` path (same as ⌘B).
- The injected native-chrome script now also adds an `openclaw-native-nav` class; `layout.css` visually retires the floating web expand button under that class using a skip-link pattern (`opacity: 0`, revealed on `:focus-visible`) rather than `display: none`, so the collapse focus-restoration path in `app-host.ts` and keyboard/screen-reader access to an in-page expand control keep working.
- Version skew stays graceful in both directions: older apps never add the class so the web fallback button keeps working, and older web bundles ignore the class and keep their own floating control (the native button's event is simply unhandled there).

## User Impact

Mac app users get a native, always-available sidebar toggle next to the back/forward buttons — matching Safari/Notes conventions — instead of a bordered web button crowding the traffic lights. Collapsing and expanding the navigation sidebar now works from the titlebar in both directions. Keyboard and screen-reader users keep an in-page expand control. Browser users see no change.

## Evidence

- Offscreen render of the new titlebar (traffic lights → sidebar toggle → back/forward, borderless, evenly spaced): https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-titlebar-sidebar-20260711/titlebar-after.png
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter DashboardWindowSmokeTests`: 25/25 pass locally (macOS-only surface), including the extended `dashboard titlebar hosts sidebar and history controls` test asserting Safari ordering, borderless style, enabled state, a resolvable SF Symbol image, and a frame wide enough for all three controls, plus the chrome-script test asserting the new `openclaw-native-nav` capability class.
- `./scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` and `./scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: clean.
- Testbox (Blacksmith via Crabbox, `tbx_01kx88fctssqntsv9ggta8rk9x`): `pnpm check:changed` plus `pnpm test ui/src/app/app-host.test.ts` — exit 0, 9/9 tests pass; CSS follow-up validated with a path-scoped `pnpm check:changed -- ui/src/styles/layout.css` on the same lease.
- New web unit test: native toggle event flips `navCollapsed` both ways through the existing navigation-surface path.
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): initial run flagged the `display: none` focus-restoration regression; fixed via the skip-link pattern above and re-reviewed clean.

target.title: fix(cron): abort superseded reconciliation hooks
target.body:
Fixes #104363

AI-assisted implementation; maintainer-reviewed and source-verified.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators projecting OpenClaw cron wakes into an external scheduler could retain a stale projection when a startup callback was still retrying during cron reload.

The newer `cron_reconciled` callback was serialized behind the stale callback, so it could not promptly abort the older durable host write or adopt the replacement scheduler.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each reconciled scheduler snapshot now owns an `AbortSignal`. Arming a newer scheduler or closing the Gateway aborts the previous signal immediately, and the replacement reconciliation dispatches without waiting behind stale observer work.

The public hook context and safe projection example carry that lifecycle-owned signal through durable acceptance. The change does not turn observation hooks into readiness-critical services and does not add a second cron authority.

## User Impact

Scale-to-zero and external-scheduler integrations can supersede stale cron projections promptly during reload. A slow or retrying prior callback no longer hides the current scheduler snapshot.

## Evidence

- Regression: a held startup callback receives an aborted signal while reload receives and completes the exact replacement scheduler without waiting.
- Invalidation regression: shutdown/explicit invalidation aborts an active snapshot.
- Focused Testbox proof: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-cron-reconciled.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-gateway.test.ts` (19 assertions passed).
- Current-head Testbox `check:changed` gate passed.
- Fresh structured Codex autoreview: clean; no accepted or actionable findings.

target.title: fix(web-search): align credential presence with usable providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

- Provider-scoped manifest env detection now first reads the selected bundled web-search provider's public contract env vars, then falls back only to same-provider manifest setup/auth env metadata when a public contract is unavailable.

target.title: fix(secrets): register secret targets for installed-origin plugins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#104320 (P1, regression of #82621/#82798): the secret target registry built its plugin-derived entries from **bundled-origin records only** (`target-registry-data.ts` filtered `record.origin === "bundled"`). When the Exa web providers moved out of bundled origin into an installed plugin package, their config targets (`plugins.entries.exa.config.webSearch.apiKey`) vanished from the gateway's known-target registry — `secrets.resolve` rejects the CLI-discovered target with `unknown target id`, and `infer web search` fails on an unresolved SecretRef before provider I/O, even though the plugin is loaded, enabled, and `secrets audit` reports full resolvability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Per the triage's best-solution shape ("build the known-target registry from active installed-plugin manifest metadata, while preserving plugin enablement, manifest-first laziness, strict allowed-path scoping, and provider-specific ownership"):

- Web-provider and config-contract secret target entries now come from **every active plugin manifest record**, exactly as channel-contract entries already did (they never filtered by origin — the bundled-only filter on the other two families was the inconsistency).
- Scoping is unchanged and stays manifest-owned: an entry is only created for a plugin that declares the web-provider contract **and** marks the config path sensitive in its own manifest hints, or declares the path in `configContracts.secretInputs`. A non-bundled origin cannot widen target paths beyond its own declared contracts, and no plugin runtime is loaded (metadata snapshot only — laziness preserved).
- No hard-coded provider ids, no validation weakening: `isKnownSecretTargetId` remains a closed registry; the registry just covers what's actually installed.

## User Impact

Users of installed (non-bundled) provider plugins with SecretRef-backed credentials — the Exa split being the shipped example — get working `infer web search`/`web fetch` credential resolution again instead of a hard `INVALID_REQUEST` from the gateway.

## Evidence

**Executed real-handler before/after** (the issue's exact `secrets.resolve` params driven through the real `createSecretsHandlers` handler, with an installed-origin Exa manifest record in the metadata snapshot):

| | result |
|---|---|
| current `main` | `ok: false` — `INVALID_REQUEST: invalid secrets.resolve params: unknown target id "plugins.entries.exa.config.webSearch.apiKey"` (byte-identical to the issue's report) |
| this PR | `ok: true` — validation passes, resolution proceeds |

**Regression test** (`target-registry-data.current-snapshot.test.ts`): an installed-origin (`origin: "global"`) record with the web-search contract + sensitive hint + declared secretInput produces the registry entry and `isKnownSecretTargetId` accepts it. **Fails on prior head** with `expected [ 'auth-profiles.api_key.key', …(37) ] to include 'plugins.entries.exa.config.webSearch.apiKey'`.

**Validation:** full `src/secrets` suite **553/553**; `tsgo:core` 0; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

Fixes #104320

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: feat(anthropic): add claude-haiku-4-5 to claude-cli catalog
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Claude CLI catalog and setup allowlist do not include `claude-haiku-4-5`, so OpenClaw users running the local Claude CLI backend cannot select the full Haiku 4.5 model ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds Haiku 4.5 to:

- the Claude CLI default allowlist and aliases
- the Claude CLI catalog label, using the existing 200K default context
- the static plugin manifest with a 200K context window, 64K max output, and 1568px image input
- the Claude CLI setup/migration expectations so existing configuration flows seed the model

Fable is intentionally left to #101453. Mythos is intentionally excluded because current `main` exposes it through the direct Anthropic provider rather than the Claude CLI backend.

## User Impact

`openclaw models list --all --provider claude-cli` can expose `claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5`. Setup/config migration seeds the ref, and both `haiku-4.5` and `claude-haiku-4-5` normalize to the full model id.

## Evidence

### Authenticated OpenClaw-to-Claude-CLI turn

Verified on Windows with Claude Code 2.1.206, using the exact PR head `61dd215e53d50dcefe78b99075ef9764e241b6cf` (`OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (61dd215)`). The OpenClaw state/config was isolated for the proof; the existing Claude Code subscription login was reused. No credentials, session ids, local paths, or hashes are included below.

Catalog probe:

```console
$ pnpm openclaw models list --all --provider claude-cli --json
{
  "key": "claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5",
  "name": "Claude Haiku 4.5 (Claude CLI)",
  "input": "text+image",
  "contextWindow": 200000,
  "available": true,
  "missing": false
}
```

Agent probe used the current canonical configuration shape: model `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` with model-scoped `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`.

```console
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main \
    --model anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 \
    --thinking off \
    --message "Return exactly OPENCLAW_HAIKU_AGENT_PROOF_OK and nothing else." \
    --json
```

Redacted result:

```json
{
  "payload": "OPENCLAW_HAIKU_AGENT_PROOF_OK",
  "executionTrace": {
    "winnerProvider": "claude-cli",
    "winnerModel": "claude-haiku-4-5",
    "attempts": [
      {
        "provider": "claude-cli",
        "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
        "result": "success"
      }
    ],
    "fallbackUsed": false,
    "runner": "cli"
  },
  "completion": {
    "finishReason": "stop",
    "stopReason": "completed",
    "refusal": false
  }
}
```

The live backend log independently recorded `provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5` for the successful turn.

### Static and CI proof

- Plugin manifest parses successfully and contains exactly one new Fable/Haiku/Mythos-family Claude CLI row: `claude-haiku-4-5`
- Verified manifest metadata: 200K context, 64K max output, 1568px image input
- Node 24 syntax checks passed for the changed TypeScript files
- Scoped `git diff --check` passed
- [GitHub CI run 286641](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29104973348) passed on the exact head; CodeQL, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, and iOS Periphery also passed

target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Live Feishu service proof (`2026-07-11T09:43:26Z`): sent a uniquely marked message to a private bot DM through the real Feishu API. After Feishu accepted attempt 1, the proof harness deliberately threw `ECONNRESET` to simulate a lost response. The production retry wrapper made attempt 2 with the same UUID; Feishu returned the same message ID, and a real chat-history query found exactly one matching delivered message.

```json
{
  "environment": "real Feishu API and private bot DM",
  "controlledFailure": "ECONNRESET thrown after Feishu accepted attempt 1",
```

target.title: fix(discord): add timeouts to directory lookup requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord directory, user allowlist, and channel allowlist lookup requests could hang indefinitely when Discord API fetches stalled before headers or during response body reads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Directory lookup callers now pass a focused 10 second timeout into the existing Discord API helper. The helper keeps the timeout alive through both `fetch()` and bounded response body reading, then clears it after the request attempt settles.

## User Impact

Discord configuration and lookup flows fail quickly when Discord API lookup calls stop responding, instead of blocking target resolution and directory browsing.

## Evidence

Exact head after normal merge from `upstream/main`: `c1e37ab5beb0c38a40632c43f4aa72bce32cc6a3`. The merge was a normal merge commit; no rebase or force-push was used.

Validation run:

```text

-> 2 files passed, 22 tests passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/resolve-users.test.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.test.ts
-> 2 files passed, 21 tests passed

-> clean

node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/discord/src/api.ts extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts extensions/discord/src/directory-live.ts extensions/discord/src/directory-live.test.ts extensions/discord/src/guilds.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-users.ts
-> clean
```

Controlled stalled Discord API proof run:

```text

```

- Normal Discord directory lookup succeeds before and after the stalled cases.
- A channel lookup that stalls before response headers aborts in about 10 seconds and closes the server-side request/response.
- A channel lookup that stalls while reading the JSON response body also aborts in about 10 seconds and closes the server-side request/response.
- This exercises the production Discord directory lookup runtime and the shared Discord API helper rather than a unit-only mocked stream.

- This is controlled-network runtime proof, not a live Discord API outage reproduction.
- Remote Testbox/Crabbox proof was unavailable in this environment because no working `crabbox` binary was present; this used the documented narrow local fallback plus GitHub CI.

target.title: refactor(agents): converge CLI tool terminal reason onto run-termination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot and live CLI runners each derived the same terminal decision — `timed_out` / `cancelled` / `failed` for tools when a run ends — with different logic:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts` (one-shot) read the abort signal's lifecycle fields, then only recognized `FailoverError` timeouts; a `TimeoutError`-shaped or `AbortError`-shaped run error without an aborted signal classified as `failed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (live) only sniffed error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) and never consulted the abort signal.

Because the live path trusted the delivered error's name alone, a run timeout whose abort reason reached the turn as a generic `AbortError` (or a non-`Error` timeout reason, which `createAbortError` cannot preserve) was reported as `cancelled` instead of `timed_out`; conversely a user cancel racing a timeout-shaped provider error reported `timed_out` where the one-shot path reports `cancelled`. Same decision, two encodings, observable drift — seam 3 of #104219.

## Why This Change Was Made

Converge the derivation onto one owner, per the #104219 change shape. `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` lives in `src/agents/run-termination.ts` — the module that already owns abort→stop-reason semantics (`resolveAgentRunAbortLifecycleFields`) — and encodes one rule: abort-signal lifecycle fields are authoritative when the signal has aborted; error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) classifies otherwise. Both call-site derivations are deleted in the same change; the live turn now carries the run's real abort signal (`ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`, threaded in `createTurn`).

`terminalReason` feeds diagnostic events only (`tool.execution.error` category/reason fields), so behavior changes are contained to diagnostics classification. The per-site `errorCategory` vocabularies (`timeout/aborted/error` vs `aborted/cli_tool_incomplete/cli_tool`) intentionally differ per event source and stay site-local.

## User Impact

Tool-failure diagnostics now classify consistently across CLI runner modes:

- Live runs that hit the run timeout report `timed_out` (previously `cancelled` when the abort reason arrived as a generic `AbortError` or a non-`Error` reason).
- A user cancel racing a timeout-shaped error consistently reports `cancelled` on both paths (signal wins).
- One-shot runs with a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`-shaped run error and no aborted signal now report `timed_out`/`cancelled` instead of `failed`.

No control-flow, retry, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites and trace: old derivations at `execute.ts` (`resolveToolTerminalReason`) and `claude-live-session.ts` (`failActiveClaudeLiveTools`); live abort delivery via `createAbortError(signal.reason)` loses timeout identity for generic/non-`Error` reasons.
- Tests: table-driven matrix for `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` in `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts` (11 cases), including both drift regressions: "timeout abort wins over generic AbortError" and "cancel abort wins over timeout-shaped error".
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles` all exit 0; focused vitest green (`run-termination`, cli-runner suites — 270+ tests).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox, leases `tbx_01kx80mneqrn7dyntk6cjptc4t`, `tbx_01kx837g6z39m9kjrfkr8mvsm8`), branch rebased on latest `main`: `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known-flaky failures under full parallel shard load (`model-fallback.probe.test.ts` async log-capture assertion; `Worker exited unexpectedly` on the gateway shard); both pass in isolation on the same lease and diff — probe test 20/20 twice, full gateway shard 402 files / 6454 tests green. Neither touches this diff's surface.
- `git diff --numstat`: +43/−17 prod, +96 tests. Net prod +26 buys the single owner: both call-site derivations deleted, one closed union exported.

### Real behavior proof (ephemeral runtime)

Real `executePreparedCliRun` flow — production executor, real process supervisor spawning a real child process, real `claude-stream-json` parser — with a stub CLI backend (one JSONL `mcp_tool_use` line, then silence; no network, no API keys, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Events observed on the trusted tool-execution bus (`onTrustedToolExecutionEvent`; the public `onDiagnosticEvent` filters trusted events). One-shot path exercised; the live session consumes the same shared helper.

Timeout run (no-output watchdog → `FailoverError reason:"timeout"`), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-timeout",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-timeout",
  "durationMs": 1509,
  "errorCategory": "cli_tool_incomplete",
  "terminalReason": "timed_out"
}
```

User-cancel run (`abortController.abort()` after `tool.execution.started` → `AbortError` with aborted signal), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-cancel",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-cancel",
  "durationMs": 137,
  "errorCategory": "aborted",
  "terminalReason": "cancelled"
}
```

Branch rebased on current `main` before this update; focused tests + `tsgo:core` green post-rebase.

Part of #104219 (seam 3: CLI-runner terminal reason derivation).

target.title: fix(gateway): add per-request cancellation to prevent late node.invoke dispatch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pending plugin approval can execute dangerous `node.invoke` work after the originating Gateway request has already timed out or disconnected. This is a P1 security vulnerability (fixes #103980): the plugin approval window (120s default) exceeds the Gateway client timeout (30s default), creating a deterministic window where dangerous node commands can dispatch side effects after the caller has already observed failure.

Root cause: The TypeScript Gateway client removes its local waiter on timeout/abort but never signals cancellation to the server. The server-side WebSocket handler launches a detached promise without retaining per-request cancellation state. On persistent WebSocket connections, a client-local timeout does not close the socket, so the server never observes the cancellation boundary.

## Evidence

### Proof test results (18 tests across 3 environments)

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ PROOF-P2: pre-aborted signal immediately expires approval without waiting (54ms)
 ✓ PROOF-P1: abort during dispatch window is captured by listener guard (2ms)
 ✓ PROOF-P1: pre-aborted signal prevents any node registry invoke call (1ms)
 ✓ PROOF-race: approval cancellation wins when abort fires before decision (2ms)
 ✓ PROOF-normal: approval flow works correctly when no abort occurs (3ms)
 ✓ PROOF-deadline: request-level deadline cancels even without socket close (2ms)

 Test Files  3 passed (3) | Tests  18 passed (18) | Duration 8.56s
```

### Full test suite (57 tests)

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts

 Test Files  6 passed (6) | Tests  57 passed (57) | Duration 10.25s
```

### Cancellation matrix

| Input form | Result |
|---|---|
| Approval completes before abort | `decision: "allow-once"` — normal flow |
| Abort fires before approval decision | `decision: null` (expired via `caller-aborted`) |
| Pre-aborted signal before `request()` | `decision: null` (immediate expiry, P2 fix) |
| Abort fires between check and invoke | `REQUEST_CANCELLED` (atomic guard, P1 fix) |
| Pre-aborted signal before `invokeNode()` | `REQUEST_CANCELLED` (no transport call) |
| Request deadline fires (persistent conn) | `decision: null` (deadline cancels even without socket close) |
| Normal flow without abortSignal | Unchanged behavior — backward compatible |

### Key proof: atomic dispatch guard prevents late side effects

The listener guard registers a one-shot `abort` listener that sets `cancelledBeforeDispatch = true` **before** any dispatch. A re-check after registration closes the race window. When the abort fires between the initial check and `nodeRegistry.invoke()`, the guard catches it and **the dangerous command never reaches the transport**:

```typescript
// P1 fix: atomic dispatch guard
let cancelledBeforeDispatch = false;
const onAbort = () => { cancelledBeforeDispatch = true; };
params.abortSignal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
try {
  if (params.abortSignal?.aborted || cancelledBeforeDispatch) {
    return { ok: false, code: "REQUEST_CANCELLED", ... };
  }
  // ... dispatch ...
} finally {
  params.abortSignal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
}
```

### Key proof: request-level deadline covers persistent connections

On persistent WebSocket connections where a client-local timeout (30s) does NOT close the socket, the server adds a request-level deadline timer using `MAX_PLUGIN_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS`. When this deadline fires, it aborts the per-request controller, expiring any pending approval even though the socket is still alive:

```typescript
// In message-handler.ts:
const requestDeadlineTimer = setTimeout(() => {
  cancelRequest("request-deadline-exceeded");
}, MAX_PLUGIN_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS);
```

### Key proof: pre-abort expiry prevents dangling approvals

AbortSignal does not replay past events. If `abortSignal.aborted` is already `true` when `addEventListener("abort")` is called, the listener never fires. The fix checks `abortSignal.aborted` before registering the listener and immediately expires the approval:

```typescript
// P2 fix: check before listener registration
if (params.abortSignal.aborted) {
  manager.expire(record.id, "caller-aborted");
  return { id: record.id, decision: null };
}
```

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.ts` | Atomic dispatch guard + pre-abort expiry + signal propagation |
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts` | 6 proof tests covering all cancellation scenarios |
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts` | 3 new cancellation regression tests |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts` | Request-level deadline + cancelRequest() + .finally() cleanup |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/shared-types.ts` | `abortSignal` in `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` |
| `src/gateway/server-methods.ts` | Forward `abortSignal` to handler invocation |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts` | Pass `abortSignal` to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` |

---

## Summary

**Updated to address ClawSweeper review findings (Round 3):**
- ✅ [P1] Make cancellation atomic with node dispatch — abort listener guard + re-check after registration
- ✅ [P2] Check for already-aborted signal before awaiting approval — immediate expiry on pre-abort
- ✅ [P1] Cancel timed-out requests, not only closed sockets — request-level deadline timer
- ✅ [P1] Preserve request dispatch error handling — removed empty catch
- ✅ Forward `abortSignal` through `handleGatewayRequest` → `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` → handler invocation
- ✅ Pass `abortSignal` from `node.invoke` handler to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` to `createApprovalRuntime`
- ✅ Add `.finally()` cleanup for per-request socket close listener
- ✅ Add 6 proof tests + 3 regression tests

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API /contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Fixes #103980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — abortSignal is optional parameter
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Diagram

```
Before fix:
Client --timeout--> removes local waiter
Server ---------------> awaits approval (120s) -----> allows -----> node.invoke executes ❌

After fix:
Client --timeout/abort/close--> fires AbortSignal
Server --sees abort--> expires approval -----> blocks node.invoke ✅
Signal flow: WebSocket → handleGatewayRequest → node.invoke handler → applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy
             └→ createApprovalRuntime (pre-abort check)
             └→ invokeNode (atomic guard: check → listener → re-check → dispatch)
```

---

Fixes #103980

target.title: fix(discord): keep voice diagnostics bounded when ffmpeg errors are multibyte
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users playing Discord voice audio could receive ffmpeg failure diagnostics that exceed the existing 8,192-byte cap when ffmpeg emits multibyte stderr text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord voice playback boundary now retains stderr as bytes and decodes the retained prefix safely after ffmpeg exits. This keeps the existing diagnostic cap accurate without changing playback, configuration, or channel behavior.

## User Impact

Discord voice playback failures keep a bounded, readable ffmpeg diagnostic even when the underlying error text contains multibyte characters.

## Evidence

- Current head: `71fc6655daae1a2496fbc49159ecc544086222b6`.
- Claim proved: Discord voice ffmpeg failure diagnostics are capped at 8,192 raw stderr bytes and decoded without a replacement character when a multibyte UTF-8 sequence crosses the cap.
- Real ffmpeg transcript: `ffmpeg-win-x86_64-v7.1.exe -hide_banner -f lavfi -i anullsrc -filter_complex_script <utf8-filter-script> -f null -` produced a failing ffmpeg child process with `stderrByteLength: 24377`, `retainedBytes: 8192`, `decodedByteLength: 8191`, `replacementCount: 0`, `decodedEndsWithReplacement: false`, and `nonAsciiCount: 4004`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/audio.test.ts` — passed: 1 file, 7 tests.
- `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 extensions/discord/src/voice/audio.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/audio.test.ts` — passed.
- `node_modules\.bin\oxlint.CMD extensions/discord/src/voice/audio.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/audio.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` — completed with no accepted or actionable findings.

target.title: fix(feishu): add 30 s request timeout to streaming-card API calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where all six outbound CardKit and tenant-token requests in
`extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without
a `timeoutMs` deadline. If the Feishu API endpoint accepts a TCP connection but
never completes the HTTP response (stalled server, network middlebox, proxy delay),
the affected call blocks indefinitely and pins a gateway request lane open.

The critical path is `getToken()`: tenant-token refresh is called before every
CardKit request, so a single stalled token endpoint blocks the entire streaming-card
reply pipeline for a running agent turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` exposes a top-level `timeoutMs` parameter that applies a hard
abort deadline to the underlying request. Adding `FEISHU_STREAMING_CARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`
and wiring it to all six call sites in one constant covers every streaming-card path
without touching callers.

The 30-second value matches the sibling pattern already used across the codebase
(e.g. `extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts`, `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts`,
`extensions/mattermost/src/api.ts`).

`extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` was checked and is not affected: its
`fetchFeishuJson` helper receives `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)`
through the caller's `init`, providing equivalent protection via a different mechanism.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Feishu API endpoint leaves tenant-token refresh or any CardKit
request pending indefinitely. No timeout error is surfaced; the streaming-card reply
lane is blocked until the process is restarted.

**After:** Every streaming-card API request fails with an abort/timeout error after
30 seconds. The caller receives a concrete error, the lane is released, and the gateway
can continue processing other messages.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/feishu-streaming-card-timeouts`  
Base: `upstream/main`  
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

```
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token fallback lifetime when the process clock is invalid
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > treats an invalid process clock as a streaming token cache miss
 ... (7 more)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

target.title: fix(agents): honor Anthropic Retry-After in auto-retry backoff (#103849)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the default Anthropic Messages transport, a 429 response with a server `Retry-After` header was turned into a plain `Error` with no status or cooldown attached, so no component in the retry path could honor the server's window. Auto-retry fell back to fixed exponential backoff and, with `maxRetries: 3`, all retries could land inside a still-active rate-limit window and fail the turn.

Closes #103849

## Why This Change Was Made

The bespoke Anthropic fetch client is not a Stainless-style SDK, so the parsed `Retry-After` was discarded before reaching any retry owner. Fixing this correctly requires the server cooldown to reach **every** retry owner — the in-turn `AgentSession.prepareRetry`, the embedded-runner failover, and the auth-profile cooldown — as **one consistent value**.

## The closed `ServerRetryAfter` representation

A server cooldown has three meaningful states, so it is modelled as a closed discriminated union (in `packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`) rather than a `number` that overloads `Infinity` as an over-limit sentinel:

```ts
export type ServerRetryAfter =
  | { kind: "seconds"; seconds: number } // finite server cooldown
  | { kind: "unbounded" };               // overflowed / unparseably-large header
// undefined = no usable Retry-After
```

An earlier `number`-with-`Infinity` shape let finite-only downstreams silently drop the over-limit case (this is exactly the defect the prior review cycles kept surfacing in different layers). The closed union makes every consumer handle `unbounded` explicitly — TypeScript exhaustiveness enforces it — so the over-limit signal can never be lost.

## Changes (threaded end to end)

- **Transport** (`anthropic-transport-stream.ts`): non-OK responses throw with `httpStatus` and a `ServerRetryAfter` built from the canonical `parseRetryAfterSeconds` (an overflowed header → `{ kind: "unbounded" }`).
- **Extraction** (`transport-stream-shared.ts`): the `ServerRetryAfter` union is carried onto the `AssistantMessage` as a validated closed object (no `Infinity` in a number field).
- **In-turn retry** (`llm/utils/retry.ts` `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs`): finite cooldown ≤ `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` is honored as a lower bound; a finite cooldown above it, or `unbounded`, returns `null` (stop in-turn retry → fallback). `maxRetryDelayMs` is now the **only** in-turn sleep ceiling.
- **Embedded failover** (`assistant-failover.ts`): `unbounded` (and finite > 60s) never triggers a same-model short-window retry; it routes to profile rotation and passes the union to the profile-failure mark.
- **Auth-profile cooldown** (`auth-profiles/usage.ts`): a finite cooldown extends the profile window; `unbounded` holds the profile for the maximum timer-safe window (`MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`) instead of collapsing to the ordinary first-failure backoff — closing the "profile eligible during an unknown provider cooldown" gap.

## User Impact

Anthropic 429s with a `Retry-After` within the configured tolerance now delay retries by at least the server window (rate-limited turns wait it out and can succeed). Cooldowns beyond the tolerance — including malformed/overflowed headers — fail fast for fallback and hold the auth profile for the full unknown window, instead of retrying inside it.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof (real managed transport + real resolver + real embedded routing).** A real Node HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header, driven through the real `createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn()` (real `buildGuardedModelFetch`); the propagated closed union is fed into the real `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` (default `maxRetryDelayMs=60000`) and the real `isShortWindowRateLimitMessage` failover router:

```
== Path A: managed transport -> AssistantMessage.retryAfter -> resolveAutoRetryDelayMs (max=60000) ==
  retry-after: 30           -> retryAfter={"kind":"seconds","seconds":30}  delay=30000ms
  retry-after: 120          -> retryAfter={"kind":"seconds","seconds":120} delay=null (stop in-turn retry -> fallback)
  retry-after-ms overflow   -> retryAfter={"kind":"unbounded"}             delay=null (stop in-turn retry -> fallback)
== Path B: embedded failover routing (isShortWindowRateLimitMessage) ==
  {seconds:30}  -> sameModelShortRetry=true
  {seconds:120} -> sameModelShortRetry=false
  {unbounded}   -> sameModelShortRetry=false  (routes to profile rotation)
```

Before this fix (origin/main) the same 429 yields no status/cooldown and a fixed 2000ms backoff.

**Focused tests (cross-layer, incl. overflow → profile).**
- `retry.auto-retry-delay.test.ts` — finite lower-bound, boundary at max, reject > max, reject `unbounded`, honor > 60s when the operator raises the max.
- `provider-transport-fetch.test.ts` — canonical parser incl. overflow → `Infinity`.
- `transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — the `unbounded` union survives extraction; resolver rejects it.
- `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — a 429 with an overflowed `retry-after-ms` surfaces `retryAfter={kind:"unbounded"}` through the real transport.
- `auth-profiles/usage.test.ts` — **an over-limit (unbounded) cooldown holds the profile for `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`** (the overflow-header-to-profile regression), and a finite cooldown extends the window.

```
$ npx vitest run <transport + retry + failover + auth-profile suites>
 Test Files  11 passed (11)
      Tests  723 passed (723)
```

target.title: fix(agents): respect provider default thinking level over global thinkingDefault
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron agentTurn jobs using Ollama models produce empty responses when `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is configured, because the global default unconditionally overrides the provider's own default of `"off"`.

- **Problem**: `resolveThinkingDefault()` checks `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` before the provider-specific default, so when a user has `thinkingDefault: "low"` (common for Claude), Ollama receives a non-`"off"` thinking level → `think: true` in the Ollama API → model consumes 100% of output tokens on reasoning → empty `content` → "Agent couldn't generate a response"
- **Solution**: Resolve the provider-specific default first, then only apply the global `thinkingDefault` when the provider does not explicitly default to `"off"`
- **What changed**: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts` (reorder evaluation in `resolveThinkingDefault()`), new test file `src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts`
- **What did NOT change**: Per-model `params.thinking` priority, Claude hardcoded special cases, the Ollama provider plugin, or any behavior for providers without an explicit default

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #104212

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is set to enable thinking for the primary model (usually Claude), the global default unconditionally overrides every provider's own default thinking level. For Ollama, which explicitly defaults to `"off"` in `extensions/ollama/provider-policy-api.ts`, this forces `think: true` in the Ollama API request, causing models like Qwen3.5-4B to consume all output tokens on reasoning and produce zero visible content.

The same Ollama workflow works correctly when no global `thinkingDefault` is set, or when `params.thinking` is explicitly configured per model.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` must not override provider-specific defaults that are `"off"`
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/ollama-respect-default-thinking-104212`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm tsgo:core      # type check
npx oxfmt --check src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # format check
npx oxlint --deny-warnings src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # lint check
pnpm test src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts --run  # unit tests
pnpm check:import-cycles  # cycle check
```

- Evidence after fix (real runtime invocation via `resolveThinkingDefault()`):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "import { resolveThinkingDefault } from './src/agents/model-thinking-default.js'; ..."

Real Behavior Evidence — PR #104248 / Fixes #104212
Environment: Node v22.19.0, linux
========================================
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=low                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=adaptive                result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=off                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | No global default                                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=adaptive                     result=adaptive (expected adaptive)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=low                          result=low (expected low)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.7 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.8 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=low + global=adaptive         result=low (expected low)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=off + global=low              result=off (expected off)
========================================
10 passed, 0 failed
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  2. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  3. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "low"` → `"low"` (per-model override works)
  4. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "off"` → `"off"` (per-model override works)
  5. Unknown provider + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"low"` (no provider default, global applies)
  6. Claude Opus 4.7 + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (hardcoded special case preserved)
  7. No global default → returns provider default

- What was not tested: Real Ollama end-to-end with actual model inference (requires local Ollama instance with a thinking-capable model). The fix is in a pure function whose behavior is fully covered by real runtime invocation with 10/10 scenarios passing.
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission change
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All thinking levels (`off`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`adaptive`/etc.) handled by existing checks; the fix only reorders them
  - ✅ Path coverage: Single change in shared `resolveThinkingDefault()` covers cron, embedded runner (session), and subagent paths
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: No new state to clean up

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`, `resolveThinkingDefault()` checked `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` (lines 71-73) **before** `resolveThinkingDefaultForModel()` (lines 101-106), so the global config default unconditionally overrode the provider-specific default from plugin policy or catalog metadata.

Introduced by: Peter Steinberger (`steipete`) in commit `d5eec80e340` — the initial implementation of `resolveThinkingDefault()`.

## Regression Test Plan

All 9 new unit tests pass on every run. Existing `thinking-runtime.test.ts` (8 tests) continues to pass — no behavioral change for Claude models or unconfigured providers.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Ollama users who have `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` set will no longer see forced thinking mode in cron agentTurn jobs. The Ollama model will run with its default behavior (thinking off) unless explicitly configured per-model via `agents.defaults.models[].params.thinking`.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: All code paths through `resolveThinkingDefault()` — per-model override, Claude special cases, Ollama default with global config, unknown provider with global config, no global config
- Edge cases checked: Global `thinkingDefault: "off"` with provider that also defaults to "off" (result is "off" either way); global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` for unknown provider with reasoning model
- What you did NOT verify: Real Ollama E2E without a local Ollama instance

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — the only behavioral change is that providers with `defaultLevel: "off"` are no longer overridden by the global default, which is a bug fix
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The shared layer (`resolveThinkingDefault()`) is the correct boundary because all code paths (cron, session, subagent) depend on it. A cron-only fix would have been ineffective because the embedded runner independently resolves defaults.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Removing the `resolveThinkingDefault()` call from the cron path only — rejected because the embedded runner (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts:291-314`) independently resolves defaults via the same function, so the bug would reappear for non-cron paths

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: The fix was designed after reading the full call chain from `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` through `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` to `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`, confirming that a shared-layer fix was needed rather than the cron-only approach originally suggested in the issue

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users who intentionally set `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` and expect it to apply globally to all providers including Ollama.

**Mitigation**: These users can still enable thinking per-model via `agents.defaults.models["ollama/..."].params.thinking`, which takes highest priority. The previous behavior was a bug (forcing thinking on models that explicitly default to "off"), not a documented feature.

**No known breaking changes** for Claude or other providers without an explicit plugin default, as `resolveThinkingDefaultForModel()` returns a generic fallback (`"medium"` for reasoning models) that is not `"off"`, so the global default continues to apply.

---

target.title: fix(gateway): cap history when numeric limit is huge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users requesting Gateway HTTP session history with an all-digit `limit` value above JavaScript's safe integer range would receive the minimum one-message page instead of the endpoint's bounded maximum history window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct REST history query parser now keeps non-digit limits on the existing minimum fallback while capping all-digit values that exceed safe integer parsing to the existing `MAX_SESSION_HISTORY_LIMIT`. This stays inside the Gateway HTTP history boundary and does not change cursor pagination, SSE streaming, RPC schemas, or configuration.

## User Impact

Gateway HTTP history callers that pass a very large numeric limit get a bounded useful page instead of unexpectedly truncating the response to one message.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: direct REST `/sessions/:sessionKey/history` caps an all-digit limit above the safe integer range to the endpoint's bounded maximum instead of treating it as `1`.
- Current head: `d27121efce282d386fb73f04e7c2be9a5e2add02`.
- Direct Gateway HTTP proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` started `src/gateway/server.ts`, seeded a file-backed session transcript with three assistant messages, and fetched the production `GET /sessions/:sessionKey/history` HTTP route with a 100-digit `limit`.

```json
{
  "head": "d27121efce282d386fb73f04e7c2be9a5e2add02",
  "proofPath": "production src/gateway/server.ts -> GET /sessions/:sessionKey/history",
  "request": {
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/sessions/agent%3Amain%3Amain/history?limit=9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999",
    "header": "x-openclaw-scopes: operator.read"
  },
  "response": {
    "status": 200,
    "sessionKey": "agent:main:main",
    "messageCount": 3,
    "texts": [
      "first message",
      "second message",
      "third message"
    ],
    "hasMore": false,
    "nextCursorPresent": false
  }
}
```

- Focused regression test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/sessions-history-http.test.ts` passed with 1 file and 21 tests.
- Formatting: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 src\gateway\sessions-history-http.ts src\gateway\sessions-history-http.test.ts` passed.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` completed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the 100-digit `limit` query returned all three seeded history messages with `hasMore: false` and no cursor, instead of falling back to a one-message page.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the Gateway HTTP history parser, direct HTTP proof, and regression test and understand the bounded limit fix.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): use truncateUtf16Safe for web snapshot maxChars cap
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `qaWebSnapshot` can produce invalid Unicode when a page's body text contains emoji or other supplementary-plane characters near the `maxChars` truncation boundary.

`qaWebSnapshot` caps the body text returned to QA scenarios with `text.slice(0, maxChars)`. QA scenarios use `maxChars: 12000` to snapshot the OpenClaw control UI, which can contain agent messages with emoji. When the page text reaches the cap with an emoji at the boundary, `slice` leaves a lone high surrogate in `snapshot.text` — which is then passed through `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` and used in `text.includes(needle)` assertions, potentially causing spurious needle misses.

**Concrete example:** `text = "abc🤖end"` (🤖 = U+1F916, two code units) with `maxChars: 4` — raw `.slice(0, 4)` keeps `"abc" + U+D83E`, a lone high surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `text.slice(0, maxChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the established pattern used across `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`, and others. No behavioral change when `maxChars` is unset or the text fits within the cap.

## User Impact

**Before:** QA scenarios that call `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` on a page whose text hits the cap with an emoji at the boundary receive `snapshot.text` with a lone surrogate, which can silently corrupt needle searches and produce unexpected scan misses.

**After:** `snapshot.text` is always well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.ts` — `qaWebSnapshot` uses `truncateUtf16Safe` for the head cap
- `qa/scenarios/ui/control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip.yaml` — live QA scenario using `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` with emoji needle checks as canonical reachability
- `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts` — exports `truncateUtf16Safe` as a proper SDK subpath for bundled plugins
- Regression: `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts` — new `does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars` case

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `qaWebSnapshot` with an active `maxChars` cap no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when page body text contains emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Canonical reachability path:** QA scenario `webSnapshot({ pageId, maxChars: 12000, … })` → `qaWebSnapshot` → `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` → `snapshot.text` → `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(snapshot.text).includes(needle)` in scenario assertion.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; no real browser needed — `bodyLocator.textContent` mock in the colocated Vitest injects the surrogate-boundary input directly into the production `qaWebSnapshot` code path.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`; no provider/channel constraints — this is plugin-local web snapshot text handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node v22, branch `fix/qa-lab-web-snapshot-utf16`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
# 1. Real Chromium integration proof (playwright-core, headless)
$ cat playwright-utf16-proof.mts   # proof script (runs from repo root)
# launches real Chromium via playwright-core, calls page.setContent() with
# emoji content, reads body.textContent(), then shows raw .slice vs truncateUtf16Safe
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts

# 2. Regression suite
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts
=== real Chromium body.textContent() proof ===
body.textContent() length (code units): 8 | value: "abc🤖end"

raw .slice(0, 4):
  length: 4
  unpaired_surrogates: true
  hex: U+0061 U+0062 U+0063 U+D83E

truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4):
  length: 3
  unpaired_surrogates: false
  value: "abc"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 RUN  v4.1.9 /Users/shen/Documents/GitHub/openclaw

 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > opens, interacts with, snapshots, and closes a page 78ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches an explicit Chromium executable override when configured 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches detected system Chromium without requiring branded Chrome 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > keeps an explicit browser channel request explicit 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > can close only selected page sessions 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > caps oversized web runtime timeouts 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  15:22:37
   Duration  535ms (transform 475ms, setup 321ms, import 44ms, tests 83ms, environment 0ms)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real headless Chromium (playwright-core, Chrome Headless Shell 149) loads `"abc🤖end"` via `page.setContent()` and `body.textContent()` returns an 8-code-unit JS string. Raw `.slice(0, 4)` leaves `U+D83E` alone (`unpaired_surrogates: true`). `truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4)` returns `"abc"` (`unpaired_surrogates: false`). target.title: feat(ui-i18n): localize Settings toolbar chrome strings (#46217 partial)
target.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `feat/i18n-settings-chrome-46217` at head 37ffcb1beb on top of upstream/main. Vite dev server started with `pnpm ui:dev` (port 5173) and a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles via the running dev server, including the new form-mode count keys added after the @clawsweeper review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm ui:i18n:sync
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm ui:dev
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config-form.search.node.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted first but the local OpenAI API key is rejected with 401, so it could not produce a review.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.
- No `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is available in this environment. A local loopback HTTP proof attempt was intentionally blocked by OpenClaw's trusted web-search SSRF guard, so no fake local endpoint was used as live Parallel proof.

target.title: chore(ui): add mock chat fixtures for design QA
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI mock has limited curated chat state for design QA, so reviewers have to rely on ad hoc sessions when checking empty chat, longer transcripts, markdown rendering, code blocks, tables, warnings, and recoverable error copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

## User Impact

There is no production user-facing behavior change. Developers and designers can load stable mock chat sessions for future Control UI visual review.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 scripts/control-ui-mock-dev.ts`
- `pnpm dev:ui:mock -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5197`
- Browser smoke loaded these proposed mock routes and confirmed the expected fixture content:
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Anew-session`
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Aqa-coding-session`
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Aresponse-shape-showcase`
  - `/chat?session=agent%3Aopenclaw-mock%3Amarkdown-showcase`

## Screenshots

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
